source.title: Ulster Herald, 22 April 1939, p. 5 ("Local Government Elections: Nominations in Tyrone")
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: 'There were no nominations in Ballygawley, Foremass, Errigal, and Newtownsaville where Messrs. J. M'Mahon, John Kelly, Patrick M'Kelvey and John Monaghan, the sitting members will automatically retain their seats'

note: Triennial election of the Clogher rural district councillors, 1939. Nominations were received by Mr. J. F. M'Crea, deputy returning officer, and closed on Tuesday 18 April 1939: 'there are to be no contests in the 16 divisions of Clogher Rural District and Board of Guardians' (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1939, p. 5). Twelve divisions had one nomination each; in Ballygawley, Foremass, Errigal and Newtownsaville no nominations were made and the sitting members retained their seats. The only change was Aughnacloy Rural (Robert Elliot for Henry Montgomerry). No party labels are printed. No poll was held; the folder date is the provisional Tyrone polling day. No nomination was received; the sitting member automatically retained the seat (recorded as returned unopposed, as the earlier rounds do for no-nomination divisions). Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
